privacy.title: Privacy and your data
privacy.description: What this platform holds about you, the consent stored on your account, and exactly what an erasure would and would not remove.
privacy.accessDescription: A subject access request (GDPR Art. 15) returns everything this platform's database holds about you, table by table. Each request is written to the audit trail, because handing over one person's data is an event worth a record.
privacy.accessError: Your data could not be prepared.
privacy.incompleteDescription: At least one store that holds data about you could not be read, so this is not the whole of what is held. The platform names it, and says why:
privacy.sectionsDescription: One row for each table that holds at least one record about you. The file you can download carries the records themselves.
privacy.linkActor: Names you as its author or owner
privacy.emptyTablesToggle: Tables searched that hold nothing about you ({count})
privacy.emptyTablesNote: These were searched too. They are listed so that an empty answer is something you can see rather than something you have to take on trust.
privacy.limitationsDescription: Stated by the platform itself, in its own words, rather than summarised here:
privacy.consentDescription: The consent columns held on your account row, read out of your own data export.
privacy.consentPending: Request your data above to see the consent stored on your account. There is no other way to read these columns.
privacy.consentNotCollected: No screen in this product sets these consent columns, so they hold whatever your account was created with. They are shown because they are stored about you, not because they record a decision you were offered.
privacy.consentEmailNote: is the consent you can change: which emails reach you. Saving it is what stamps the date above.
privacy.erasureDescription: What a request to be erased (GDPR Art. 17) removes, and what it deliberately leaves in place.
privacy.erasureNotSelfServiceTitle: Erasure is not a button on this page
privacy.erasureNotSelfService: Erasure here is irreversible and cannot be undone, so this platform lets nobody erase their own account - not employees, and not administrators. The request is raised by you and carried out by someone who is accountable for it.
privacy.erasureHowToAsk: Send the details below to your organisation's administrator or data protection contact. This platform has no form that lodges the request for you, and this page will not pretend otherwise.
privacy.erasureDeletedNote: These rows are removed from the database.
privacy.erasureDeletedNotifications: every message sent to you, its text, and the delivery details recorded when you opened it.
privacy.erasureDeletedSurveyDrafts: surveys you started writing and never submitted.
privacy.erasureDeletedUserDemographics: your answers to your employer's demographic questions.
privacy.erasureDeletedInvitationDemographics: demographic values assigned in advance to an invitation addressed to you.
privacy.erasureAnonymisedTitle: Kept, with the link to you severed
privacy.erasureAnonymisedNote: The rows survive; what identifies you in them does not.
privacy.erasureAnonymisedResponses: your survey answers. Your user id, IP address, browser and session are cleared, so no row leads back to you - but the answers themselves and the demographic values attached to them stay. They are not deleted because every climate score and benchmark your employer has already acted on is a total over these rows, and removing yours would silently restate figures that have been published.
privacy.erasureAnonymisedUsers: your account row. Your email is replaced with an address that can never receive mail, your name and password are removed, your department and manager are cleared, the account is deactivated and every session it holds against this platform stops working. The row itself survives, because business records and the audit trail point at it.
privacy.erasureRedactedNote: The row stays because something counts it; the columns naming you do not.
privacy.erasureRedactedMicroclimateInvitations: invitations to a microclimate: your address and its access token are overwritten.
privacy.erasureDeletedSurveyAuditLogs: the survey change trail. Your rows are deleted outright, not overwritten - so the per-survey history no longer records that those changes were made at all. The platform-wide audit trail above is the one that survives.
privacy.erasureRedactedSurveyInvitations: invitations to a survey: your address and its access token are overwritten. The row is the denominator of a response rate that has already been reported.
privacy.erasureRedactedUserInvitations: the invitation that brought you here: your address, its token and its payload are overwritten. Who sent it is kept, because that was their act and not yours.
privacy.erasureKeepsAudit: The platform-wide audit trail (audit_logs) is kept in full, under Art. 17(3)(b) and (e). It is how this platform can show who did what to whose data - including who ran your erasure - so deleting it would defeat the mechanism the right itself depends on. The per-survey change trail is a separate table and is deleted; it is listed above.
privacy.erasureKeepsAttribution: Business records you created - surveys, reports, action plans, templates - keep their attribution. The account they point at is a pseudonym afterwards.
privacy.erasureKeepsFreeText: Free text is not scrubbed. An open-ended answer, an audit payload or an invitation note can name a person inside prose, and no automated rule finds that reliably. Those columns are kept exactly as written.
privacy.erasureKeepsSnapshots: Historical demographic snapshots are kept. They are records that have already been reported on, and removing a row would change totals that were published.
privacy.erasureKeepsOtherTenants: Rows matched by your email address are erased only inside the organisation whose administrator ran the erasure. An address is not unique across organisations, and another company's invitation is that company's record.
privacy.erasureKeepsTracking: The separate tracking service keeps its own database and this platform cannot reach it. Anything held there has to be dealt with by hand - your data export says the same thing.
privacy.erasureKeepsTrackingSession: A session token issued before the erasure keeps working against that tracking service until it expires, at most 24 hours later. Against this platform it stops working immediately.
